items.title: New Supply Chain Attack Compromises Tens of Thousands of GitHub Repositories
items.one_liner: A supply chain campaign compromised tens of thousands of GitHub repositories with malicious workflows that harvest credentials from commit histories.
items.summary: Security researchers at Socket discovered a software supply chain attack affecting tens of thousands of GitHub repositories, including organization-owned projects such as Uber's athenadriver. The campaign, a variation of the GhostAction tactic, relies on two compromised GitHub accounts—'henrywoo' and 'kitao'—to push a malicious GitHub Actions workflow disguised as a security audit. The workflow automatically executes during routine tasks, stealing API keys, tokens, and historical credentials from repository files and Git history before exfiltrating them over HTTP to an external server at 193.32.204[.]199. Because the attackers systematically targeted all repositories they had access to rather than filtering by activity, even inactive projects were compromised.
items.bottom_line: A widespread GitHub supply chain attack has compromised tens of thousands of repositories via malicious CI/CD workflows that exfiltrate sensitive secrets.

items.title: The One Thing Every AI Agent Framework Agrees On - Mislav Ivanda, Daytona｜AI Engineer
items.one_liner: AI agent frameworks have quietly converged on a standard three-call sandbox contract, making execution boundary selection critical for production safety.
items.summary: In a talk on AI agent execution boundaries, Daytona developer experience engineer Mislav Ivanda highlights that major frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, and Google ADK have converged on a shared three-call sandbox contract consisting of sandbox creation, code execution, and sandbox deletion. Ivanda argues that teams should select their isolation execution boundary before choosing an agent framework, as execution environments cannot be cheaply swapped later. He outlines three isolation tiers, warning that local execution guardrails and allow-lists remain vulnerable because agents can still open network sockets and modify files once code execution is permitted.
items.bottom_line: Development teams must choose secure container isolation tiers before picking an agent framework, as local-execution proofs of concept present severe production security risks.

claims.support_span: Africa’s biggest refinery attracted about 5.85 trillion naira ($4.1 billion) of applications for shares in the continent’s largest public offering to date, almost three times the amount it sought to raise...

claims.text: The company received $1.9 billion from Nigerian investors and $2.1 billion from international buyers.
claims.support_span: ...received about $1.9 billion in inquiries from investors in its home country of Nigeria and a further $2.1 billion from international buyers...
